title: A Three-Fluid Model of Dissipation at Surfaces in Superconducting Radiofrequency Cavities
authors: Matthias Liepe Michelle M. Kelley, Sean Deyo, Nathan Sitaraman, Danilo B. Liarte, Tomás Arias, James P. Sethna, Thomas Oseroff
abstract: Experiments on superconducting cavities have found that under large RF fields the quality factor can improve with increasing field amplitude, a so-called ``anti-Q slope.'' We numerically solve the Bogoliubov-de Gennes equations at a superconducting surface in a parallel magnetic field, finding at large fields there are surface quasiparticle states with energies below the bulk superconducting gap that emerge and disappear as the field cycles. Modifying the standard two-fluid model, we introduce a ``three''-fluid model where we partition the normal fluid to consider continuum and surface quasiparticle states separately. We compute dissipation in a semi-classical theory of conductivity, where we provide physical estimates of elastic scattering times of Bogoliubov quasiparticles with point-like impurities having potential strengths informed from complementary \textit{ab initio} calculations of impurities in bulk niobium. We show, in this simple yet effective framework, how the relative scattering rates of surface and continuum quasiparticle states can play a role in producing an anti-Q slope while demonstrating how this model naturally includes a mechanism for turning the anti-Q slope on and off.
summary: This paper addresses the unexplained 'anti-Q slope' in superconducting cavities by developing a novel three-fluid model. It separates normal fluid excitations into surface-bound and continuum states, calculating dissipation using Bogoliubov quasiparticle scattering rates. The model successfully demonstrates that the differential scattering rates between these two populations can generate the observed field-dependent quality factor anomaly.
main_problem: The paper investigates the anomalous 'anti-Q slope' observed in superconducting radiofrequency (SRF) cavities, where the quality factor increases with the accelerating RF field amplitude.
main_result: The authors propose a three-fluid model that successfully explains the anti-Q slope by showing that the relative scattering rates between surface-localized and continuum quasiparticle states can induce this effect.
method: The analysis involves solving the Bogoliubov-de Gennes equations numerically and employing a semi-classical theory of conductivity, modifying the standard two-fluid model.
model_or_system: The system is superconducting niobium cavities operating under large RF fields. The model is a 'three-fluid' extension of the standard two-fluid model, separating the normal fluid into distinct continuum and surface quasiparticle components.
key_observables: Quality factor (Q) vs. accelerating field, local superconducting gap $\Delta(z)$, and the relative scattering rates ($	au_b/	au_c$) of bound vs. continuum quasiparticles.
important_parameters: Niobium parameters ($E_F = 5.32$ eV, $\Delta_0 = 1.5$ meV, $\lambda = 40$ nm), operating temperature ($T=2$ K), and RF frequency ($\omega = 1.3$ GHz).
main_assumptions: The model assumes that bound states ($E_n < \Delta_0$) are governed by different scattering dynamics than continuum states ($E_n \ge \Delta_0$), necessitating the three-fluid approach.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the partitioning of the normal fluid into bound and continuum components, the weakening of the superconducting gap at the surface, and the predicted Q vs. accelerating field curves based on different scattering rate assumptions.
paper_structure: The paper builds from identifying the experimental anomaly (anti-Q slope) to developing the theoretical framework (three-fluid model using BdG equations) to calculate dissipation via scattering rates, culminating in the prediction of the anti-Q slope mechanism.
why_interesting: This work provides a detailed, microscopic mechanism for macroscopic superconducting performance anomalies, linking quantum quasiparticle dynamics (surface states) to measurable RF cavity parameters (Q-factor).
